question: A 5-year-old HIV-positive child on ART is being evaluated for possible TB after exposure to a smear-positive household contact. His Mantoux (TST) shows 6 mm of induration at 72 hours. How should this result be interpreted?

answers.text: Negative — the cut-off for all children is ≥10 mm regardless of immune status

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The 10 mm cut-off applies to immunocompetent children (including those with BCG). A lower threshold applies to immunocompromised children.

answers.text: Positive — the cut-off for immunocompromised children (including HIV-positive) is ≥5 mm

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. For immunocompromised children (HIV-positive, on immunosuppressants, severely malnourished), a Mantoux of ≥5 mm is considered positive. The standard threshold of ≥10 mm applies to immunocompetent children. This child's 6 mm reading is positive and warrants further workup.

answers.text: Indeterminate — readings of 5–9 mm require a repeat TST in 4 weeks

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. There is no 'indeterminate' zone requiring repeat testing in standard guidelines. The threshold drops to ≥5 mm in immunocompromised children; this reading is positive.

answers.text: Positive only if the child has no BCG scar — BCG vaccination makes 6 mm a false positive in all children

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. BCG is factored into interpretation for immunocompetent children (threshold ≥10 mm). For HIV-positive children, the threshold is ≥5 mm regardless of BCG status.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the Mantoux interpretation section. Key thresholds: ≥10 mm for immunocompetent children; ≥5 mm for immunocompromised children (HIV, malnutrition, immunosuppressants).
Correct. The Mantoux threshold for immunocompromised children (including HIV-positive) is ≥5 mm. The standard threshold of ≥10 mm applies to immunocompetent children with or without BCG.
